voiceover: Isn't the Trinity a contradiction — one equals three? It would be, if Christians said God is one person and three persons, or one God and three gods, in the same sense. But that isn't the doctrine. The Trinity says God is one in being — one 'what' — and three in persons — three 'whos': Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Those are different categories. So there's no contradiction — any more than one triangle having three sides is a contradiction. It's a mystery — something we couldn't have guessed and can't fully exhaust. But a mystery is not a contradiction. And it wasn't invented to be clever. It was forced by the evidence: Scripture insists there is only one God, yet calls the Father, the Son, and the Spirit each fully God. The Trinity is simply what you get when you refuse to drop either truth.
